## Day at a Glance

| | |
|---|---|

---

## Morning

After breakfast at the masseria, drivers shuttle the group to **Otranto** — an ancient town perched on a rocky bluff overlooking the Adriatic Sea. Its roots are the Greek city Hydrus; its coastal position facing the Balkans and Greece runs through its history as a Roman port. UNESCO designated it a "messenger site of peace."

A local guide leads a walking tour of the town's most important historic sites.

## Afternoon

Free time in Otranto's historic center — explore, browse shops, or find a seaside café for lunch on your own.

Return to the masseria in the afternoon. Options: pool, cool drink under the olive trees, or arrange a shuttle to a local beach.

## Evening

The evening excursion gathers in the courtyard at **17:00** for pickup. The first stop is **Il Faro**, the lighthouse, followed by **Porto Badisco** for bar food, drinks, good company, and sea views. The group returns to **Masseria dei Monaci** around **19:30**.

---

## Daily Retrospective

Otranto’s great surprise was the **Tree of Life** in the cathedral — not a small decorative mosaic, but an entire medieval pavement world of stories, beasts, scripture, and legend underfoot. The cathedral was the day’s clear highlight: the most remarkable mosaic Dan had ever seen, covering the whole floor section by section and still walked on by visitors.

Lunch was in the harbor overlooking the Adriatic: fresh vegetables, sea bream, a light torte, and plenty of fruit. The setting matched the meal — clean, bright, and maritime rather than heavy.

The evening moved back out toward the coast. Everyone met in the courtyard at **17:00** for pickup, then stopped first at **Il Faro**, the lighthouse at Punta Palascia / Cape Otranto — the easternmost point of Italy — before continuing to **Porto Badisco** for bar food, drinks, good company, and wide sea views. The return to Masseria dei Monaci was scheduled for **19:30**, a compact coastal coda to a day already shaped by Otranto’s cathedral, harbor, and Adriatic edge.

![Il Faro at Punta Palascia / Cape Otranto, the easternmost point of Italy, looking out over the Adriatic.](images/punta-palascia-lighthouse-easternmost-italy.jpeg){fig-alt="White lighthouse below a dry coastal hillside, with the blue Adriatic Sea stretching to the horizon at Italy's easternmost point."}

---

## Practical Notes

- Lunch is on your own — budget €15–25; seafood cafés along the waterfront
- Cobblestone streets throughout the historic center — comfortable walking shoes
- Albania is visible on a clear day from the Adriatic coast
- Evening pickup: **17:00** in the courtyard
- Evening stops: **Il Faro** at Punta Palascia / Cape Otranto — the easternmost point of Italy — then **Porto Badisco** for bar food, drinks, friends, and sea views
- Return to Masseria dei Monaci: **19:30**
